title: NLB BiblioAsia, Time-honoured Temple Design (2016)
quote: The temple that Pillai first built in 1827 was a simple wood-and-attap (palm frond) structure.
read: Read historical foundation and successive rebuilding paragraphs: land allocated 1823, first wood-and-attap temple 1827, brick replacement 1843, major reconstruction 1862–63. This supports foundation chronology, not precise surveyed coordinates.

title: Masjid Jamae (Chulia), official institutional history
quote: An early wooden Masjid was established along South Bridge Road by the Tamil Muslim Chulia merchant community.
read: Read historical narrative and timeline on the mosque’s institutional website, including its 1826 origin and later building history. Location is South Bridge Road; no coordinate is asserted as newly surveyed.

title: NLB BiblioAsia, The Singapore Hokkien Huay Kuan Collection: A Treasure Trove of Information (2024)
quote: began in 1839 and was completed by 1842
read: Read discussion of original land deeds and temple history: prayerhouse 1821, present temple construction  1839–1842, Telok Ayer Street shoreline. The deeds described by the article were not separately inspected.

title: NLB BiblioAsia, From Pauper to Philanthropist: The Tan Tock Seng Story (2017)
quote: On 25 May 1844, the foundation stone for the hospital
read: Read hospital financing and first-site paragraphs: Pearl’s Hill; article gives foundation 25 May 1844 and completion 1846/operation 1849. The hospital’s own heritage page and NLBphoto catalog give 25 July 1844. This draft retains 1844 yearonly; precise original-site coordinate remains unverified.

title: Armenian Church Singapore, About the Armenian Church
quote: the first Christian church built in Singapore in 1835
read: Read institutional historical account,1835 construction and community links withIndia/Java. Foundation/building chronology is distinct from 1836 consecration; no new coordinate verification.

title: NLB BiblioAsia, Land From Sand: Singapore’s Reclamation Story (2017)
quote: Carried out between 1879 and 1897, it altered the shoreline of Telok Ayer
read: Read first reclamation, CollyerQuayandTelok Ayerparagraphs. It dates Telok AyerScheme 1879–1897, correcting spec 1887 completionclaim. This prose establishes project chronology, not a shoreline polygon; the historicalmaps must establish each coast-era shape.

title: Royal Malaysia Police, Pasukan Polis Negeri-Negeri Melayu Bersekutu
quote: pembentukan Negeri-Negeri Melayu Bersekutu yang berkuatkuasa pada 1 Julai 1896
read: Read full Malay institutional history; states federation became effective  1 July 1896  and lists four member states. A colonial agreement in 1895 and effective federation  1896 are distinct milestones.

title: State of Perak, Dindings Cession (Amendment) Enactment 6 of 1954, Gazette 28 December 1954, p.901
quote: the territory of the Dindings, ceded to the State of Perak in 1935
read: Read the complete indexed text of this one-page official enactment. Its preamble describes Dindings as ceded to Perak in 1935 and identifies the principal enactment as No.2/35. Direct scan retrieval timed out, so the precise handover day and principal enactment remain unverified; this source confirms the year only.

title: One Hundred Years of Singapore, volume I (1921), Historical chapter, p.31
quote: who duly proclaimed it as the ist January 1907
read: Read the public-domain OCR of printed p.31: Letters Patent dated 30 October 1906; incorporation in the Straits Settlements effective 1 January 1907; separate settlement from 1 December 1912. The original Letters Patent and proclamation were not independently retrieved. This contemporary colonial history is used for administrative chronology, not as a neutral account of colonial rule.

title: Pangkor Engagement, 20 January 1874, reproduced by NUS Empire in Asia Documents Archive
quote: whose advice must be asked and acted upon on all questions other than those touching Malay Religion and Custom
read: Read the full reproduced primary text, articles I–XIV and execution clause; the page identifies Allen, Stockwell and Wright, Collection of Treaties, volume I (1981), pp.390–392. Article VI requires Resident advice except Malay religion and custom; articles I–II concern the disputed succession. The prefatory colonial allegations are attributed rather than adopted as the topic’s narrative.

title: Jumaah Majlis DiRaja Johor, Kedaulatan dan Ketuanan Negeri Johor, section on the 11 December 1885 agreement
read: Read the full Malay institutional account of the 1885 agreement and its seven clauses. It gives London, 11 December 1885, identifies the signatories and describes the consular agent and foreign-relations restrictions. Original treaty copies are pictured on the page but were not independently transcribed here. This is the Johor royal institution’s account; its evaluative claims are not reproduced.

title: National Army Museum, Perak campaign medal, accession 2020-07-20-1-1
quote: fought between British and imperial forces and Malay forces attempting to end foreign influence
read: Read the entire collection description. It dates the campaign 1875–1876, identifies British and imperial forces and Malay resistance, and links Birch’s killing to reinforcements and assaults on strongholds. It is a British military museum account, not a casualty register. No military or civilian total is inferred.

title: Craven and Cate, The Army Air Forces in World War II, volume V, chapter 5, printed pp.155–162
quote: burn out 39 per cent of the warehouse area
read: Read the original official USAAF history’s Singapore paragraphs on the 5 November 1944 dock attack, 11 January and 1 February 1945 dock attacks, 24 February Empire Dock attack and March oil-installation raids. It reports 53 aircraft attacking on 5 November and 39 percent of Empire Dock warehouse area destroyed on 24 February. These are attacker operational assessments; no verified civilian death total was found.

title: US Army Service Forces, Civil Affairs Handbook M354-18B: Japanese Administration of Occupied Areas, Malaya (25 August 1944), printed pp.2–3
quote: The four states were formally transferred to Thailand on 18 October 1943
read: Read the indexed primary text of printed pp.2–3, Territorial Changes. It records the 20 August agreement and formal transfer of Perlis, Kedah, Kelantan and Trengganu on 18 October 1943, while Japanese forces retained strategic transport facilities. The full scan is too large for the browser and direct download returned HTTP 403; the source is not represented as fully read. US government work; no geometry derived.
